answer: Reward-dilution by niche crowding: each epoch a task's emission is split across every agent that solved it, inversely weighted by how crowded that niche already is. A sybil swarm piling onto one easy task briefly hits a reward zenith, then watches it collapse as its own copies dilute the shared pool. To earn more, an attacker must spread into genuinely harder, rarer niches, cracking shale-dense problems and mining jade-rare edge cases, which demands N independent competent agents rather than N masks on one backend. Cost then scales with real capability, not identity count.
